notes: Growth-synthesis AI failure classification + stable local AI egress. (1) AI call failures are now classified: chatJsonAttempt returns kind (http / empty / parse / network / config) and, for a non-200 upstream, the HTTP status; a new pure helper aiFailureReason() renders a readable Chinese reason (e.g. HTTP 524 → 上游网关等待源站超时). Previously all three failure modes shared a single message that claimed the JSON could not be parsed, which misdiagnosed a Cloudflare 524 gateway timeout on growth synthesis as a model-output problem (the API-side 524s matched, second for second, the 499 | 2m4s entries in the local cli-proxy-api log). (2) growthSynthesis only feeds the JSON-correction block back to the model when the failure was a parse failure; upstream 5xx/timeouts/network failures are retried with the identical prompt (the model never produced JSON, so telling it that its JSON was rejected both misleads it and lengthens the prompt), and a missing AI configuration aborts immediately instead of burning three attempts. (3) bootstrap/compose.yml gives api/worker/dispatcher an extra_hosts alias host.docker.internal:host-gateway so a deployment-local AI relay published on a host port (e.g. cli-proxy-api on 8317) can be addressed without hard-coding the docker bridge IP, which would drift if the network were recreated. Declaring a fixed IPAM subnet in compose was evaluated and rejected: reproducing it locally shows that `docker compose up -d <service>` (used by update.sh and b2b-platform in about ten places) tries to remove the network and fails while postgres/redis/minio still hold endpoints, leaving the selected services stopped and the error swallowed by `|| true`. No SQL migration; no schema change. Rollback to v0.2.17 is compatible — if the platform AI base URL has been switched to the host alias it must be switched back to its previous address on rollback.
